sources.title: National Museum of Lithuania: Curonians, tribal culture, jewellery and dress
sources.note: Institutional catalogue description dates formation to fifth/early sixth century CE. This makes the imported500BCEto200CE label retrospective, not evidence of a medieval Curonian state.

sources.title: Lithuanian Universal Encyclopedia: Curonian language
sources.note: Rašto paminklų nepaliko: no written monuments left; names/toponyms and later linguistic traces, language lost by sixteenth/early seventeenth century. Do not substitute modern Kursenieki.

sources.title: Andrejs Vasks, Latvian National Encyclopedia: Paplaka hillfort
sources.note: Original indexed full entry, excavator account, Nozīme pētniecībā: sunken building2x3m, clay lining/daub,32pots, radiocarbon361to204BCE. Direct fetch502, indexed exact query site:enciklopedija.lv/skirklis/189056 Paplakas datēta.

sources.title: Algimantas Merkevičius and Lijana Remeikaitė: The Kurmaičiai microregion in the Early and Roman Iron Age
sources.note: 2012, printed118to119 English summary. Three communities and opposite-bank zoning are hypotheses; five test pits did not find prehistoric houses.

sources.title: Lijana Muradian: First AMS radiocarbon dating of western Lithuanian barrow cremations
sources.note: 2022 Estonian Journal of Archaeology26(2),157to183. Printed167 nonadult Šlikiai grave;171table2 date396to206calBCE;170Kveciai1047to1260CE intrusive grave. Twelve samples, not twelve whole skeletons.

sources.title: Algimantas Merkevičius and Lijana Muradian: The Earliest Horse Remains in Lithuanian Burial Sites
sources.note: Volume16(2015), online2016 research abstract, five barrows/three cemeteries, partial unburnt horse remains with cremated humans, Late Bronze/Early Iron Age.

sources.title: Eugenijus Jovaiša: Dauglaukis grave84 and finds
sources.note: Excavator record and plan,1991 excavation, child of unidentified sex, iron pin/amber bead, broad70to260CE date; possible disturbance and now poorly preserved objects.

sources.title: Anna Bitner-Wróblewska, Audronė Bliujienė and Wojciech Wróblewski: Following the Traces of the Lost Ėgliškiai-Anduliai Curonian Cemetery
sources.note: Printed79footnote7 Hadrian coins117to138;82 rediscovery2002;84 late first/second-century flat inhumations with joined stone circles. Broad cemetery chronology extends beyond map.

sources.title: Karolis Minkevičius and colleagues: Adaptability and resilience, farming practices in Lithuania during the Roman Iron Age
sources.note: 2024 Archaeologia Baltica31,44to62, introduction/49 earliest rye and oats100to200calAD;57 proposed infield/outfield farming. Regional dataset largely inland, not a sample of every coastal household.

sources.title: Inga Doniņa-Kalniņa, Latvian National Encyclopedia: Curonians
sources.note: Original indexed full entry. Mid-eleventh-century northern expansion into Finnic areas, economy, ironworking,1253partition and1267conquest. Avoid rigid ethnic boundaries and speculative class population ratios.

sources.title: Rokas Kraniauskas: Curonian settlement on the grounds of Palanga manor
sources.note: Excavation report2010, published2011pp45to60. English abstract P1 tenth/eleventh-century house with two hearths,kitchen and loom annex; P2 upper building twelfth/thirteenth, deliberately excluded.

sources.title: Palanga Municipality: archaeological monuments and finds
sources.note: Lithuanian figure captions7to9: Viking-period ship fastenings; stone gaming piece, possible chess fragment, horse-metacarpal skate; woman/girl burial late tenth/early eleventh century. English machine translation calls gaming stone bone; original Lithuanian controls.

sources.title: Latvian National Encyclopedia: Talsi hillfort
sources.note: Original indexed research section: tenth/fourteenth-century occupation,ninebuildingphases,tenth-century double timber defenses and houses beside wall. Not all early inhabitants assigned Curonian identity.

sources.title: Jonas Genys: Trade routes and trade centres in Western Lithuania during the early Middle Ages
sources.note: Printed141to154, especially142to143 coastal routes and uncertain glass-bead origins,143eleventh-century Impiltis ingot hoard. PDF OCR misreads surname as Gents.
